entries.rationale: Under the direct profile this parameter operation is owned by the native rclcpp node / rclcpp::Parameter; a fresh-process differential and the test_prove_parameter_authority.py coverage tripwire prove the exact public contract, C++ payload representation (converters/serializers poisoned at zero), and stock-identical behavior, with a CPU-first stock/direct local-parameter hot-path benchmark on record (scripts/benchmarks/run_local_parameter_benchmark.py, docs/backend-selection.md). Direct-C++ authority, not a performance claim; the reviewed dual-arch CPU gate is open.

Direct-C++ authority, not a performance claim; the reviewed dual-arch CPU gate is open.

DirectNode.create_rate(frequency, clock=None) validates frequency > 0 (ValueError, matching stock's message) and honors only the node's own clock or None; it returns a DirectRate(rclpy.timer.Rate) anchored at the node clock's now() plus one period, sleeping on the node's NativeClockSleeper with the rclcpp::Rate fixed-rate algorithm (including its catch-up guard) rather than stock's Timer+threading.Event design -- a documented behavioral superset, since it sleeps correctly with or without a spinning executor. destroy_rate(node, rate) destroys the rate and returns True. Verified live: isinstance(rclpy.timer.Rate); period cadence with no per-gap drift, matched against an in-process stock Rate/Timer/executor sibling's own cadence; sim-time pacing that resolves only once a native /clock publish crosses the anchored deadline; a context shutdown waking an in-flight sleep with ROSInterruptException; and a destroyed rate's sleep() raising RuntimeError (test/_direct_cpp_rate_helper.py, test/_stock_rate_peer.py, test/test_direct_rate.py). CPU-first evidence is measured in scripts/benchmarks/run_clock_timer_benchmark.py's rate-sleep workload. Direct-C++ authority, not a performance claim; the reviewed dual-arch CPU gate is open.

DirectNode.create_rate(frequency, clock=None) validates frequency > 0 (ValueError, matching stock's message) and honors only the node's own clock or None; it returns a DirectRate(rclpy.timer.Rate) anchored at the node clock's now() plus one period, sleeping on the node's NativeClockSleeper with the rclcpp::Rate fixed-rate algorithm (including its catch-up guard) rather than stock's Timer+threading.Event design -- a documented behavioral superset, since it sleeps correctly with or without a spinning executor. destroy_rate(node, rate) destroys the rate and returns True. Verified live: isinstance(rclpy.timer.Rate); period cadence with no per-gap drift, matched against an in-process stock Rate/Timer/executor sibling's own cadence; sim-time pacing that resolves only once a native /clock publish crosses the anchored deadline; a context shutdown waking an in-flight sleep with ROSInterruptException; and a destroyed rate's sleep() raising RuntimeError (test/_direct_cpp_rate_helper.py, test/_stock_rate_peer.py, test/test_direct_rate.py). CPU-first evidence is measured in scripts/benchmarks/run_clock_timer_benchmark.py's rate-sleep workload. Direct-C++ authority, not a performance claim; the reviewed dual-arch CPU gate is open.

DirectNode.create_rate(frequency, clock=None) validates frequency > 0 (ValueError, matching stock's message) and honors only the node's own clock or None; it returns a DirectRate(rclpy.timer.Rate) anchored at the node clock's now() plus one period, sleeping on the node's NativeClockSleeper with the rclcpp::Rate fixed-rate algorithm (including its catch-up guard) rather than stock's Timer+threading.Event design -- a documented behavioral superset, since it sleeps correctly with or without a spinning executor. destroy_rate(node, rate) destroys the rate and returns True. Verified live: isinstance(rclpy.timer.Rate); period cadence with no per-gap drift, matched against an in-process stock Rate/Timer/executor sibling's own cadence; sim-time pacing that resolves only once a native /clock publish crosses the anchored deadline; a context shutdown waking an in-flight sleep with ROSInterruptException; and a destroyed rate's sleep() raising RuntimeError (test/_direct_cpp_rate_helper.py, test/_stock_rate_peer.py, test/test_direct_rate.py). CPU-first evidence is measured in scripts/benchmarks/run_clock_timer_benchmark.py's rate-sleep workload. Direct-C++ authority, not a performance claim; the reviewed dual-arch CPU gate is open.

DirectNode.create_timer() builds a real rclcpp::GenericTimer on the node's own ROS clock (sim-time-aware, matching stock's create_timer(clock=None) default) via rclcpp_kit's create_clock_timer, entering the Python callback once per firing with no message conversion, serialization, or per-firing data copy. clock=None and clock=node.get_clock() are both honored; a standalone or foreign clock, or any unexpected keyword argument, fails closed before entity creation (create_timer's signature now matches stock's exactly, with no **options catch-all). Verified live: inspection (is_ready/time_until_next_call/time_since_last_call) matching stock semantics; a frozen, never-published /clock leaves a sim-period timer never firing while wall time passes well beyond it; advancing /clock in explicit steps fires the callback only once sim time crosses the period; a use_sim_time=False node's timer fires on system time within a bounded wall interval; and destroying the facade stops delivery while the executor keeps spinning (test/_direct_cpp_timer_helper.py, test/_direct_cpp_clock_timer_helper.py, test/test_direct_clock_timer.py). CPU-first evidence for this exact route is measured in scripts/benchmarks/run_clock_timer_benchmark.py. Direct-C++ authority, not a performance claim; the reviewed dual-arch CPU gate is open.

Verified live: isinstance(rclpy.timer.Rate); period cadence with no per-gap drift, matched against an in-process stock Rate/Timer/executor sibling's own cadence; sim-time pacing that resolves only once a native /clock publish crosses the anchored deadline; a context shutdown waking an in-flight sleep with ROSInterruptException; and a destroyed rate's sleep() raising RuntimeError (test/_direct_cpp_rate_helper.py, test/_stock_rate_peer.py, test/test_direct_rate.py). CPU-first evidence is measured in scripts/benchmarks/run_clock_timer_benchmark.py's rate-sleep workload. Direct-C++ authority, not a performance claim; the reviewed dual-arch CPU gate is open.

DirectNode.create_rate(frequency, clock=None) validates frequency > 0 (ValueError, matching stock's message) and honors only the node's own clock or None; it returns a DirectRate(rclpy.timer.Rate) anchored at the node clock's now() plus one period, sleeping on the node's NativeClockSleeper with the rclcpp::Rate fixed-rate algorithm (including its catch-up guard) rather than stock's Timer+threading.Event design -- a documented behavioral superset, since it sleeps correctly with or without a spinning executor. destroy_rate(node, rate) destroys the rate and returns True. Verified live: isinstance(rclpy.timer.Rate); period cadence with no per-gap drift, matched against an in-process stock Rate/Timer/executor sibling's own cadence; sim-time pacing that resolves only once a native /clock publish crosses the anchored deadline; a context shutdown waking an in-flight sleep with ROSInterruptException; and a destroyed rate's sleep() raising RuntimeError (test/_direct_cpp_rate_helper.py, test/_stock_rate_peer.py, test/test_direct_rate.py). CPU-first evidence is measured in scripts/benchmarks/run_clock_timer_benchmark.py's rate-sleep workload. Direct-C++ authority, not a performance claim; the reviewed dual-arch CPU gate is open.

DirectNode.create_timer() builds a real rclcpp::GenericTimer on the node's own ROS clock (sim-time-aware, matching stock's create_timer(clock=None) default) via rclcpp_kit's create_clock_timer, entering the Python callback once per firing with no message conversion, serialization, or per-firing data copy. clock=None and clock=node.get_clock() are both honored; a standalone or foreign clock, or any unexpected keyword argument, fails closed before entity creation (create_timer's signature now matches stock's exactly, with no **options catch-all). Verified live: inspection (is_ready/time_until_next_call/time_since_last_call) matching stock semantics; a frozen, never-published /clock leaves a sim-period timer never firing while wall time passes well beyond it; advancing /clock in explicit steps fires the callback only once sim time crosses the period; a use_sim_time=False node's timer fires on system time within a bounded wall interval; and destroying the facade stops delivery while the executor keeps spinning (test/_direct_cpp_timer_helper.py, test/_direct_cpp_clock_timer_helper.py, test/test_direct_clock_timer.py). CPU-first evidence for this exact route is measured in scripts/benchmarks/run_clock_timer_benchmark.py. Direct-C++ authority, not a performance claim; the reviewed dual-arch CPU gate is open.

DirectNode.create_rate(frequency, clock=None) validates frequency > 0 (ValueError, matching stock's message) and honors only the node's own clock or None; it returns a DirectRate(rclpy.timer.Rate) anchored at the node clock's now() plus one period, sleeping on the node's NativeClockSleeper with the rclcpp::Rate fixed-rate algorithm (including its catch-up guard) rather than stock's Timer+threading.Event design -- a documented behavioral superset, since it sleeps correctly with or without a spinning executor. destroy_rate(node, rate) destroys the rate and returns True. Verified live: isinstance(rclpy.timer.Rate); period cadence with no per-gap drift, matched against an in-process stock Rate/Timer/executor sibling's own cadence; sim-time pacing that resolves only once a native /clock publish crosses the anchored deadline; a context shutdown waking an in-flight sleep with ROSInterruptException; and a destroyed rate's sleep() raising RuntimeError (test/_direct_cpp_rate_helper.py, test/_stock_rate_peer.py, test/test_direct_rate.py). CPU-first evidence is measured in scripts/benchmarks/run_clock_timer_benchmark.py's rate-sleep workload. Direct-C++ authority, not a performance claim; the reviewed dual-arch CPU gate is open.

Direct-C++ authority, not a performance claim; the reviewed dual-arch CPU gate is open.

DirectNode.create_rate(frequency, clock=None) validates frequency > 0 (ValueError, matching stock's message) and honors only the node's own clock or None; it returns a DirectRate(rclpy.timer.Rate) anchored at the node clock's now() plus one period, sleeping on the node's NativeClockSleeper with the rclcpp::Rate fixed-rate algorithm (including its catch-up guard) rather than stock's Timer+threading.Event design -- a documented behavioral superset, since it sleeps correctly with or without a spinning executor. destroy_rate(node, rate) destroys the rate and returns True. Verified live: isinstance(rclpy.timer.Rate); period cadence with no per-gap drift, matched against an in-process stock Rate/Timer/executor sibling's own cadence; sim-time pacing that resolves only once a native /clock publish crosses the anchored deadline; a context shutdown waking an in-flight sleep with ROSInterruptException; and a destroyed rate's sleep() raising RuntimeError (test/_direct_cpp_rate_helper.py, test/_stock_rate_peer.py, test/test_direct_rate.py). CPU-first evidence is measured in scripts/benchmarks/run_clock_timer_benchmark.py's rate-sleep workload. Direct-C++ authority, not a performance claim; the reviewed dual-arch CPU gate is open.

CPU-first evidence for this exact route is measured in scripts/benchmarks/run_clock_timer_benchmark.py. Direct-C++ authority, not a performance claim; the reviewed dual-arch CPU gate is open.

DirectNode.create_rate(frequency, clock=None) validates frequency > 0 (ValueError, matching stock's message) and honors only the node's own clock or None; it returns a DirectRate(rclpy.timer.Rate) anchored at the node clock's now() plus one period, sleeping on the node's NativeClockSleeper with the rclcpp::Rate fixed-rate algorithm (including its catch-up guard) rather than stock's Timer+threading.Event design -- a documented behavioral superset, since it sleeps correctly with or without a spinning executor. destroy_rate(node, rate) destroys the rate and returns True. Verified live: isinstance(rclpy.timer.Rate); period cadence with no per-gap drift, matched against an in-process stock Rate/Timer/executor sibling's own cadence; sim-time pacing that resolves only once a native /clock publish crosses the anchored deadline; a context shutdown waking an in-flight sleep with ROSInterruptException; and a destroyed rate's sleep() raising RuntimeError (test/_direct_cpp_rate_helper.py, test/_stock_rate_peer.py, test/test_direct_rate.py). CPU-first evidence is measured in scripts/benchmarks/run_clock_timer_benchmark.py's rate-sleep workload. Direct-C++ authority, not a performance claim; the reviewed dual-arch CPU gate is open.

Under the direct profile, create_subscription translates stock's SubscriptionEventCallbacks, ContentFilterOptions, and QoSOverridingOptions into the suite's event_callbacks dict, content_filter tuple, and qos_overriding bool respectively, composing all three in the same call; the public contract and mirror-equal signature are unchanged, and a live per-RMW proof exists for each. event_callbacks: deadline, liveliness, incompatible_qos, matched, and message_lost fire live on Cyclone with field values matching an identical stock scenario run side by side; every event callable is exception-contained and in-flight-counted under a public MultiThreadedExecutor (proven: a raising event callback does not std::terminate the process, and destroying a subscription mid-dispatch of its own event callback is safe across 50 iterations); incompatible_type fails closed as UnsupportedEventTypeError (rmw_cyclonedds_cpp has no DDS listener for it) -- a deliberate, disclosed stricter-than-stock divergence from stock's own silent dead-handler registration. content_filter_options always fails closed through this product today with the new ContentFilterUnsupportedError: direct_cpp is hard-gated to rmw_cyclonedds_cpp only, and that RMW has no content-filter implementation at all, so there is no live positive-filtering path reachable at this layer; the filtering mechanism itself is proven live and working on Fast DDS at the suite layer, independent of this gate. qos_overriding_options is honored only for the exact default policy set (HISTORY, DEPTH, RELIABILITY; no callback; no entity_id); live proof shows the qos_overrides.<topic>.subscription.{history,depth,reliability} parameters are declared and an override actually changes the created subscription's effective QoS, while any custom subset/callback/entity_id fails closed with a clear not-supported error instead of silently applying the default set. Disclosed divergences (all deliberate, none silent): (1) event-bearing entities carry no default handler for events the caller did not set, unlike stock's own default incompatible-QoS warning logger and incompatible_type registration for non-overridden events; (2) an event-bearing, content-filtered, or qos-overriding subscription cannot use the subscription_shared_lease CPU optimization and falls back to the regular managed construction path (a performance, not correctness, divergence); (3) Subscription.event_handlers retains the original callables for introspection parity, but its shape differs from stock's own list of QoSEventHandler/Waitable objects, since dispatch here is fully native and no Python-side Waitable ever exists; (4) the event callback receives the native rclcpp C++ status struct by reference (field-name-compatible with stock's rclpy info dataclass, but not the same Python type -- a cold-path status payload, not application data, left unconverted); (5) qos_overriding_options is not wired on create_publisher at all and stays rejected exactly as before this wave, because the suite has no publisher-side attachment point for QosOverridingOptions -- a documented, stricter-than-stock suite gap, deferred pending a suite-side change. create_publisher's own event_callbacks work has no ledger row to carry this authority: its direct-profile signature lacks stock's type annotations and return type (a pre-existing signature-mirror gap unrelated to this work), so the ledger's structural comparison keeps that row at missing_mismatch regardless of behavioral evidence -- create_subscription's signature is already mirror-equal and carries the promotion for all three capabilities. No CPU/performance claim is made; this is a correctness/authority classification only.

DirectNode.create_timer() builds a real rclcpp::GenericTimer on the node's own ROS clock (sim-time-aware, matching stock's create_timer(clock=None) default) via rclcpp_kit's create_clock_timer, entering the Python callback once per firing with no message conversion, serialization, or per-firing data copy. clock=None and clock=node.get_clock() are both honored; a standalone or foreign clock, or any unexpected keyword argument, fails closed before entity creation (create_timer's signature now matches stock's exactly, with no **options catch-all). Verified live: inspection (is_ready/time_until_next_call/time_since_last_call) matching stock semantics; a frozen, never-published /clock leaves a sim-period timer never firing while wall time passes well beyond it; advancing /clock in explicit steps fires the callback only once sim time crosses the period; a use_sim_time=False node's timer fires on system time within a bounded wall interval; and destroying the facade stops delivery while the executor keeps spinning (test/_direct_cpp_timer_helper.py, test/_direct_cpp_clock_timer_helper.py, test/test_direct_clock_timer.py). CPU-first evidence for this exact route is measured in scripts/benchmarks/run_clock_timer_benchmark.py. Direct-C++ authority, not a performance claim; the reviewed dual-arch CPU gate is open.

Verified live: isinstance(rclpy.timer.Rate); period cadence with no per-gap drift, matched against an in-process stock Rate/Timer/executor sibling's own cadence; sim-time pacing that resolves only once a native /clock publish crosses the anchored deadline; a context shutdown waking an in-flight sleep with ROSInterruptException; and a destroyed rate's sleep() raising RuntimeError (test/_direct_cpp_rate_helper.py, test/_stock_rate_peer.py, test/test_direct_rate.py). CPU-first evidence is measured in scripts/benchmarks/run_clock_timer_benchmark.py's rate-sleep workload. Direct-C++ authority, not a performance claim; the reviewed dual-arch CPU gate is open.

Under the direct profile, guard conditions are native rclcpp guard conditions; create_guard_condition/destroy_guard_condition/trigger are proven with callback dispatch through the containment shim and executor wake.

create_publisher delegates to the native rclcpp publisher factory; event_callbacks translation is proven by node.direct_cpp_qos_events, while qos_overriding_options stays rejected on publishers (a disclosed suite gap, not silently ignored).

DirectNode.create_rate(frequency, clock=None) validates frequency > 0 (ValueError, matching stock's message) and honors only the node's own clock or None; it returns a DirectRate(rclpy.timer.Rate) anchored at the node clock's now() plus one period, sleeping on the node's NativeClockSleeper with the rclcpp::Rate fixed-rate algorithm (including its catch-up guard) rather than stock's Timer+threading.Event design -- a documented behavioral superset, since it sleeps correctly with or without a spinning executor. destroy_rate(node, rate) destroys the rate and returns True. Verified live: isinstance(rclpy.timer.Rate); period cadence with no per-gap drift, matched against an in-process stock Rate/Timer/executor sibling's own cadence; sim-time pacing that resolves only once a native /clock publish crosses the anchored deadline; a context shutdown waking an in-flight sleep with ROSInterruptException; and a destroyed rate's sleep() raising RuntimeError (test/_direct_cpp_rate_helper.py, test/_stock_rate_peer.py, test/test_direct_rate.py). CPU-first evidence is measured in scripts/benchmarks/run_clock_timer_benchmark.py's rate-sleep workload. Direct-C++ authority, not a performance claim; the reviewed dual-arch CPU gate is open.

DirectNode.create_timer() builds a real rclcpp::GenericTimer on the node's own ROS clock (sim-time-aware, matching stock's create_timer(clock=None) default) via rclcpp_kit's create_clock_timer, entering the Python callback once per firing with no message conversion, serialization, or per-firing data copy. clock=None and clock=node.get_clock() are both honored; a standalone or foreign clock, or any unexpected keyword argument, fails closed before entity creation (create_timer's signature now matches stock's exactly, with no **options catch-all). Verified live: inspection (is_ready/time_until_next_call/time_since_last_call) matching stock semantics; a frozen, never-published /clock leaves a sim-period timer never firing while wall time passes well beyond it; advancing /clock in explicit steps fires the callback only once sim time crosses the period; a use_sim_time=False node's timer fires on system time within a bounded wall interval; and destroying the facade stops delivery while the executor keeps spinning (test/_direct_cpp_timer_helper.py, test/_direct_cpp_clock_timer_helper.py, test/test_direct_clock_timer.py). CPU-first evidence for this exact route is measured in scripts/benchmarks/run_clock_timer_benchmark.py. Direct-C++ authority, not a performance claim; the reviewed dual-arch CPU gate is open.
